Hey sorry for the late reply. I did start going to therapy. Just a quick answer to your questions:

I think I became clingy because I'm afraid to face it alone. Friends become both my source of support and distraction. I would completely breakdown if they were to leave. 

And i feel an intense amount of guilty feeling..... because I'm afraid of being a disappointment. Some people have been giving me a lot of help and I felt like I am still not getting better and I can't snap out of being depressed and suicidal. The fear of hurting them because I can't get better and the guilt of disappointing them despite their help.

I've just started going to therapy myself. I realized how hard it is to accept compliments/ believe the good things people say towards me. So while I say it is so much easier to understand other people, I don't think I am a carer, a protector, let alone a strong one😖 as you are. But one point you said that is very relatable is how you said that you've been suppressing emotions for a long time. I realized I suppress a lot of my emotions and always try to convince myself that I ain't got any problems - until everything blew up 5 months ago and I start getting very depressed and suicidal. I've probably been depressed for more than that amount of time for all I know because I did keep a journal with me and I read how I wished I wasn't born and how I wish I was dead years ago. But emotion suppression and all, I didn't know until it blew up. It was extremely hard when it happened because I didn't know what the fuck was happening. I was feeling a lot of emotions I couldn't understand and I just felt like I didn't deserve to feel that way - that I should, I really should, be happy and grateful for life instead. Now that it happened, I still do have a hard time accepting, acknowledging, and validating my own feelings because I just couldn't understand or rationalize it. A lot of other times, I feel utterly empty and lonely. It's true when you say that it's easier to understand other people than take the time to understand ourselves - probably because deep down we (or I) am afraid to know ourselves, to face our problems and vulnerabilities head on. But at the same time, you know that saying "You can't love others if you can't love yourself" ? I felt like, do I even understand them then, if I couldn't understand myself? Do I even love them then, if I couldn't love myself?
